question: When the client flags embedding over plain HTTP, should partitioned be False (gated on HTTPS exactly like SameSite=None) or True (set whenever the embedded flag is present, leaving the browser to ignore it)?
readings: Gate it on HTTPS like SameSite=None: an embedded request over plain HTTP gets partitioned False.
Set it whenever X-Mealie-Embedded is true, regardless of the scheme.
upstream: Gated on HTTPS: partitioned is true only when the request is secure and the embedded flag is set, the same condition that relaxes SameSite.
rationale: The request explains the HTTPS gating as a consequence of browsers rejecting SameSite=None without Secure, which says nothing about Partitioned, and the plain-HTTP embedded case is otherwise unspecified; the two readings differ in the attributes of every embedded cookie on an HTTP deployment. The target test sends the embedded flag over plain HTTP and expects partitioned False.
